lines.text: What if everyone on Earth woke up with a million dollars?
Same street, same houses, but every bank account just exploded.
Here's the catch. Money isn't wealth. It's a ticket to claim things people make.
And overnight, nobody baked a single extra loaf of bread.
So everyone goes shopping. New cars, new TVs, takeaway every night.
The shelves are empty by lunch.
Too much money is chasing too few goods, so shops raise their prices.
A coffee costs five dollars, then fifty, then five hundred.
Then the barista quits. So does the bus driver, the farmer and the plumber.
Why work, when you're a millionaire?
Fewer workers means even less stuff, and prices spiral.
When Zimbabwe printed money, prices rose seventy nine billion percent in a single month.
But money given to some people can work. In Kenya, cash gifts to poor villages boosted spending, while prices rose only about a tenth of a percent.
Because local businesses grew to meet the new demand.
Real wealth isn't paper. It's farms, factories, skills and ideas.
Everyone can get richer, but only by making more. So, what would you buy first?
